newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SAVINGS BANK SAYS 5 MO NET PROFIT 2.1 MLN LTL.
newsitem.headline: SAVINGS BANK SAYS 5 MO NET PROFIT 2.1 MLN LTL.

text.p: Lithuania's Savings Bank said on Wednesday that its net profit for the first five months of the year was 2.1 million litas compared to 6.4 million litas in the same period in 1996.
The bank also said that its assets stood at 1.4 billion litas at the end of May versus 1.15 billion at the beginning of 1997.
The bank also said in a statement that its net profit fell because of provisions paid by the bank to the deposit insurance fund for individual deposits kept in the bank.
The bank said it paid 3.6 million litas to the deposit fund during March, April and May.
The deposits of the bank at the end of May rose to 1.24 billion litas from 1.03 billion litas at the beginning of the year, the statement added.
It also said that 986 million litas of total deposits belonged to individual depositors at the end of May.
The bank reoorted loans at 606 million litas at the end of May compared to 505 million litas at the beginning of the year.
The 74 percent state-run bank posted a 30 million litas net profit for 1996 and 1.73 million litas net profit for the first quarter of this year.
Savings Bank is the biggest bank in terms of asstets and is the only one of the three state banks not yet slated for privatisation.

The share capital of the bank is 60 million litas but it is to do a 20 million litas share capital boost. Some six million litas of the capital rise will come from own reserves and 14 million litas from additional contributions.
